briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Weed Finds Fresh Shelf Space as D.C. Keeps the Rescheduling Door Open
briefs.top: Michigan operators are leaning into growth — a new tribal-land dispensary, a national edibles rollout, and a gubernatorial candidate courting industry cash with a pledge to gut the 24% wholesale tax — even as that tax keeps badly missing its own revenue targets. Nationally, cannabis investors are more bullish than they've been in months and Compass Pathways is barreling toward an FDA filing for psilocybin, even as a DEA judge hit pause on the Schedule III rescheduling timeline.

local.text: Hempire Collective opens on tribal land near Mount Pleasant — The family-owned, vertically integrated operator held a ribbon-cutting September 26 at its new storefront next to Soaring Eagle Casino on the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe's reservation.
Wyld's Grön 'Pearls' gummies land on Michigan shelves — The bestselling edibles line kicked off a four-state rollout, confirmed stocked at Pure Options, High Profile, and Lume locations.

JARS Cannabis turns a Michigan footprint into an Arizona takeover — The Michigan-based chain announced a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa-brand dispensaries, set to make JARS the largest retailer in Arizona.

John James rallies industry cash behind a tax-repeal promise — The GOP governor nominee is raising money from marijuana industry donors after pledging to repeal or sharply reduce the state's new 24% wholesale tax.

Wholesale tax keeps falling short, building the case for relief — The levy generated just $73.4 million in its first six months versus a $420 million annual projection, giving momentum to repeal bills already filed in Lansing.

national.text: Cannabis investors turn notably more bullish on reform — A new survey found respondents assigned 65% odds to federal rescheduling within six months, with 47% saying they're more bullish on MSOs than six months ago and none more bearish.

DEA pumps the brakes on rescheduling, but the case survives — The agency's chief judge paused the Schedule III hearing September 29 to weigh a new GAO report, with responses due October 13, though attorneys say the stay doesn't signal rescheduling is in jeopardy.

Compass Pathways closes in on an FDA filing for psilocybin — Fresh off 26-week Phase 3 data showing a durable response in treatment-resistant depression, the company is targeting a Q4 2026 NDA submission for COMP360.

Bipartisan lawmakers press the White House for Schedule III clarity — A bipartisan quartet of House members sent letters to Trump and three cabinet officials asking for guidance on the federal framework for medical cannabis.
Trulieve becomes the first plant-touching MSO on the NYSE — The company's medical-only restructuring after federal Schedule III reclassification cleared the path for its listing under ticker TRLV.
